title: Completed differential pullback to a smooth branch and its rational extension
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $S$ a finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak m$ a maximal ideal with residue field $k$, and $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $D$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] which is the local $k$-algebra at a $k$-rational point of a smooth one-dimensional curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves]. Let $\alpha:A\to D$ be a local $k$-algebra map. Put $R=\widehat A$ and $T=\widehat D$, using maximal-ideal-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and fix a complete local $k$-algebra isomorphism $T\cong k[[t]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $\widehat\alpha:R\to T$ for the induced map. Let $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$ and $L=k((t))$, with the embeddings $D\to T\to L$ and $F\to L$. Write $\Omega$ for Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and use scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change]. For $h(t)=\sum h_nt^n$ put $h'(t)=\sum n h_nt^{n-1}$; on $L$ use the quotient rule. The notation $T\,\mathrm dt$ or $L\,\mathrm dt$ denotes a free module on the displayed symbol.

There is a $T$-linear isomorphism $E:\Omega^1_{D/k}\otimes_D T\xrightarrow{\sim}T\,\mathrm dt$ with $E(\mathrm dd\otimes1)=(\iota_D(d)(t))'\,\mathrm dt$ for every $d\in D$, where $\iota_D(d)(t)$ denotes the image of $d$ in $T$. The continuous extension of the universal derivation of $D$, composed with $E$, is termwise differentiation on all of $T$. The rational map $\delta_F:\Omega^1_{F/k}\to L\,\mathrm dt$, $\mathrm dz\mapsto(z(t))'\,\mathrm dt$, is injective and induces an $L$-linear isomorphism $\Omega^1_{F/k}\otimes_F L\xrightarrow{\sim}L\,\mathrm dt$.

Let $\widehat{\mathrm d}_A:R\to\Omega^1_{A/k}\otimes_A R$ denote the continuous extension of the universal derivation, with continuity and extension understood as in [def-trf-completed-differential-extension]. The map on algebraic differentials for $\alpha$, extended to $T$ and followed by $E$, gives $\beta:\Omega^1_{A/k}\otimes_A T\to T\,\mathrm dt$. Its compatibility with completion is
$$\beta(\widehat{\mathrm d}_A(h)\otimes1)=(\widehat\alpha(h))'\,\mathrm dt\qquad(h\in R),$$
where tensor associativity identifies the source with $(\Omega^1_{A/k}\otimes_A R)\otimes_R T$.

For every continuous local presentation $R\cong k[[z_1,\ldots,z_n]]/(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$ with $g_j\in(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$, let $e_i=\widehat{\mathrm d}_A(z_i)$ and $z_i(t)=\widehat\alpha(z_i)$. Then $\beta(e_i\otimes1)=z_i'(t)\,\mathrm dt$, and, with the coefficientwise partial derivatives of [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], the Jacobian relations give
$$\sum_i (\partial g_j/\partial z_i)(z(t))\,z_i'(t)=0\qquad(1\le j\le s).$$
After extending scalars to $L$, this map agrees with the composite of the natural map $\Omega^1_{A/k}\to\Omega^1_{F/k}$ and $\delta_F$.

For every complete local $k$-algebra isomorphism $\sigma:k[[t]]\xrightarrow{\sim}k[[s]]$, put $v(s)=\sigma(t)$. It extends uniquely to a field isomorphism $\tau:k((t))\xrightarrow{\sim}k((s))$ and $v'(s)$ is a unit in $k[[s]]$. For every $h\in k((t))$ the formal chain rule is
$$\tau(h'(t))v'(s)=(\tau(h))'(s).$$
The map $\nu:h(t)\,\mathrm dt\mapsto\tau(h(t))v'(s)\,\mathrm ds$ is an invertible $\tau$-semilinear map of the rational differential modules and carries $k[[t]]\,\mathrm dt$ onto $k[[s]]\,\mathrm ds$. Under scalar transport $\omega\otimes c\mapsto\omega\otimes\sigma(c)$, with $\tau$ on rational scalars, the maps $E$, $\beta$ and $\delta_F$ just described commute with $\nu$ and their counterparts for the parameter $s$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), algebraically closed Jacobian-presentation proof paragraph and completion passage; Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), coordinate changes. Agent-formulated naturality and smooth-branch refinement; these tags do not assert the mixed completion/naturality theorem verbatim.

proof.text: Write $D=B_{\mathfrak q}$ using an affine neighbourhood of its given smooth rational point; $B$ is finite type over $k$ and $B/\mathfrak q=k$. Apply [lem-trf-completion-kahler-differential-comparison] with coefficient field $k$ and its structure section. It identifies $\Omega_{D/k}\otimes_D T$ with $\widehat\Omega_{T/k}$ and carries the extended derivation to the quotientwise universal derivation. The fixed isomorphism $T\cong k[[t]]$ induces isomorphisms on all maximal-ideal-power quotients, hence on their differential inverse limits (apply the inverse ring isomorphism to obtain the inverse maps). For one variable, [lem-trf-formal-power-series-continuous-free] identifies this limit with $T\,\mathrm dt$ and sends $\widehat{\mathrm d}(h)$ to $h'\,\mathrm dt$. Their composite is $E$ and proves both its formula on $D$ and the claimed formula for the continuous extension on all of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), completed Jacobian passage; explicit comparison and one-variable continuous-differential inputs

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] (with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, so the fibre is the curve itself), shrink the smooth curve to an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ of the point on which $\Omega_{B'/k}$ is free of some finite rank $d$. Localizing by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] makes $\Omega_{D/k}$ free of rank $d$, so $\Omega_{D/k}\otimes_DT$ is free of rank $d$ over $T$; by Step 1 it is isomorphic to $T\,\mathrm dt$, and rank of free modules over the nonzero commutative ring $T$ is invariant, so $d=1$. Let $b$ be the resulting basis of $\Omega_{D/k}$. The same localization theorem gives $\Omega_{F/k}=F b$. Write $E(b\otimes1)=u\,\mathrm dt$. Since $E$ is an isomorphism, multiplication by $u$ on $T$ is bijective, so $u$ is a unit. The map $F b\to L\,\mathrm dt$, $c b\mapsto\iota_F(c)u\,\mathrm dt$, is injective since $F\to L$ is a field embedding and $u\ne0$; after scalar extension it is multiplication by $u$ on $L$, hence an isomorphism. For $z=a/c$ with $a,c\in D$, $c\ne0$, Leibniz gives $\mathrm dz=c^{-1}\mathrm da-ac^{-2}\mathrm dc$. Its image is $(a(t)'c(t)-a(t)c(t)')/c(t)^2\,\mathrm dt=z(t)'\,\mathrm dt$. Thus this map is exactly $\delta_F$, including its asserted injectivity.

source.place: Tag 02G1 (morphisms.tex, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free); Tag 00RT (algebra.tex, lemma-differentials-localize); Tag 07PE (more-algebra.tex, lemma-derivation-extends), localization quotient rule

proof.text: The universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] applied to $a\mapsto\mathrm d(\alpha(a))$ gives the algebraic differential map. Extend scalars and compose with $E$ to obtain $\beta$. Its composite with $\widehat{\mathrm d}_A$ is continuous: the extension exists and is continuous by [lem-trf-completion-kahler-differential-comparison] for $A$, and any $R$-linear map from its target to $T\,\mathrm dt$ sends $\mathfrak m^N$ times that target into $(t)^N T\,\mathrm dt$, since $\widehat\alpha$ is local. The other map $h\mapsto(\widehat\alpha(h))'\,\mathrm dt$ is continuous: locality sends $\mathfrak m^N R$ into $(t)^N$, and coefficientwise differentiation lowers order by at most one. On $A$ both maps take $a$ to $\alpha(a)(t)'\,\mathrm dt$ by Step 1. Given $h\in R$, choose representatives $a_N\in A$ of its compatible completion coordinates; they tend to $h$ by the inverse-limit definition [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Applying the two continuous maps and using that a series in every $(t)^N$ has every coefficient zero proves their equality on $h$. Tensor associativity here sends $(\omega\otimes r)\otimes c$ to $\omega\otimes\widehat\alpha(r)c$, with inverse $\omega\otimes c\mapsto(\omega\otimes1)\otimes c$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, completion passage; continuity justified by comparison and inverse-limit representatives

proof.text: Apply Step 3 to $h=z_i$ to obtain $\beta(e_i\otimes1)=z_i'(t)\,\mathrm dt$. Let $P=k[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$ and let $\psi:P\to T$ be its presentation map followed by $\widehat\alpha$, so $\psi(Z_i)=z_i(t)\in(t)$. The map $H\mapsto(\psi(H))'$ is a $\psi$-derivation by the coefficientwise Leibniz rule. Apply [lem-trf-formal-relative-derivation-expansion] with $m=n$, target variable count $1$, and this derivation. It gives $(\psi(H))'=\sum_i\psi(\partial_iH)z_i'(t)$. Since $\psi(g_j)=0$, taking $H=g_j$ proves the displayed Jacobian relations. This uses arbitrary formal series, rather than treating the $g_j$ as polynomials.

After scalar extension to $L$, evaluate the two maps in the rational-compatibility assertion on $\mathrm da\otimes c$, $a\in A$, $c\in L$. The map through $\beta$ gives $c\,\alpha(a)(t)'\,\mathrm dt$ by Steps 1 and 3. The map through $\Omega_{F/k}$ gives $c\,\delta_F(\mathrm d\alpha(a))$, which is the same expression by Step 2. These differential symbols generate by the construction in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], so the maps agree on the entire scalar extension.

source.place: Tag 0C4D completion passage; generator calculation of rational naturality

proof.text:
An isomorphism $\sigma:k[[t]]\to k[[s]]$ sends the maximal ideal $(t)$ onto $(s)$; hence $v=\sigma(t)=s w(s)$ with $w(0)\ne0$. Consequently $v'(0)=w(0)\ne0$, and $v'$ is a unit: its inverse is obtained recursively from the coefficients, dividing by $w(0)$. Extending $\sigma$ to fractions gives the unique field isomorphism $\tau$, with $\tau(f/g)=\sigma(f)/\sigma(g)$; equality of fractions and the inverse follow by cross multiplication and the inverse of $\sigma$. Every Laurent series is $t^{-N}f(t)$ for a power series $f$, so these are precisely the stated fields. Apply [lem-trf-formal-relative-derivation-expansion] to the $\sigma$-derivation $f\mapsto(\sigma f)'$ to get $(\sigma f)'=\sigma(f')v'$ for every power series $f$. For $h=f/g$, quotient differentiation gives
$$(\tau h)'=\frac{(\sigma f)'\sigma g-\sigma f(\sigma g)'}{(\sigma g)^2}=\tau\!\left(\frac{f'g-fg'}{g^2}\right)v'=\tau(h')v'.$$
This proves the chain rule for all Laurent series, with no characteristic restriction.

source.place: Tag 0C4B, coordinate changes; Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends), fraction rule

proof.text:
Define $
u(c\,\mathrm dt)=	au(c)v'\,\mathrm ds$. Its inverse is $d\,\mathrm ds\mapsto	au^{-1}(d/v')\,\mathrm dt$, proving invertible semilinearity. Since $\sigma$ carries the power-series ring onto the power-series ring and $v'$ is a unit there, $
u$ carries the stated lattices onto each other. For $d\in D$, Step 6 gives
$$
u igl(E_t(\mathrm dd\otimes c) igr)=\sigma(c)\sigma(d(t)')v'\,\mathrm ds=\sigma(c)(\sigma(d(t)))'\,\mathrm ds=E_s(\mathrm dd\otimes\sigma(c)).$$
For rational scalars replace $\sigma$ by $	au$. The identical calculation with $d=\alpha(a)$ proves the square for $ eta$ on $\mathrm da\otimes c$, and with $d=z\in F$ proves it for $\delta_F$ on $\mathrm dz$. All differential modules are generated by these symbols by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], so these calculations prove every claimed square. Step 3 then also gives compatibility on completed elements; no additional choice of extension is involved.
